title: Skillet pizza crust
steps: Heat a cast-iron pan or pizza stone in the oven at 220 °C.
Pull it out, drizzle in 1 tsp oil, ladle the discard straight onto the hot metal and spread it thin.
Second teaspoon of oil over the top, then salt and herbs. Bake 10 min until crisp and it lifts free.
Move to a baking sheet, sauce and top it, bake another 8–10 min until bubbling.
asides: Cast iron or stone only. On a normal tray the raw starter welds itself to the surface.

title: Herb & parmesan crackers
steps: Oven to 175 °C, line a baking sheet with parchment.
Stir everything together in one bowl.
Spread as thin as you can across the parchment — thickness decides snap.
Bake 15 min, then score into squares with a pizza wheel.
Back in for 20–25 min until golden. Cool 10 min, snap apart.

title: Chocolate chip blondies
steps: Oven to 175 °C, line the tin with parchment.
Whisk the melted butter into both sugars until glossy.
Whisk in eggs, yolk, discard and vanilla until smooth.
Stir the dry ingredients through — stop as soon as the flour disappears.
Fold in the chips, spread level, bake 40–45 min to golden edges and a set middle.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting.

title: Fudgy brownies
steps: Oven to 175 °C, parchment in the tin.
Melt the butter in a pan, take it off the heat, stir in chocolate and vanilla until smooth.
Mix flour, sugar, cocoa and salt in a bowl.
Pour the chocolate in, add eggs and discard, stir until no clumps remain.
Bake 40 min — set in the centre, skewer clean. Cool fully before slicing.
asides: Overnight version: the night before, mix the flour, discard, sugar and melted butter, cover and chill up to 24 h. Add the rest and bake as above — deeper tang, easier on the gut.

title: Banana crumb muffins
steps: Oven to 175 °C, line or grease the tins.
Beat melted butter and brown sugar 5 min — this is what makes them light.
Beat in eggs, vanilla, banana and discard.
Whisk the dry ingredients separately, then add in thirds, mixing only until combined.
Rub the crumb ingredients together with your fingers.
Scoop batter into the tins, crumb on top, bake 20–25 min to a clean skewer.

title: Skillet cornbread
ingredients: 128 g butter (9 tbsp — 1 for the pan)
steps: Oven to 205 °C. Put 1 tbsp butter in a 25–30 cm cast-iron pan and slide it into the oven for 5 min.
Whisk egg, honey and sugar. Whisk in the remaining melted butter and the milk, then stir in the discard.
Whisk Maisgrieß, flour, baking powder and salt in a second bowl.
Fold dry into wet just until combined — overmixing makes it tough.
Pour into the screaming-hot pan. Bake 18–20 min. Cool 20 min before cutting.

title: Sourdough granola
ingredients: 110 g oil (½ cup — coconut or a neutral one)
steps: Oven to 175 °C. Mix nuts, oats, coconut and salt.
Stir through the honey, oil and discard until every flake is coated.
Spread on a lined tray, bake 30 min, stirring once at the halfway mark.
Fold the dried fruit in while it's warm. Cool completely, then break into clusters.
asides: The discard is the binder here — it's what gets you clusters rather than loose oats.

title: Quick discard pancakes
steps: Melt the butter and let it cool. Combine flour, salt and Natron in a big bowl.
Add discard, milk, eggs, butter and honey. Whisk just to combined — lumps are fine, a smooth batter makes flat pancakes.
Butter a medium-hot pan, ladle in about 80 ml per pancake.
Flip when the edges set and bubbles reach the middle; 1–2 min on the second side.
asides: The smallest discard cost on the list — the workhorse for a jar that's nearly empty.

title: Discard bagels
ingredients: 42 g honey or maple syrup (2 tbsp)
steps: Whisk yeast into the warm water, leave 5 min to go bubbly.
Add discard, honey, salt and flour. Knead 5–10 min to a smooth dough.
Greased bowl, covered, 60–90 min until doubled.
Divide into 8, roll into balls, poke a thumb through and stretch the hole wide — it shrinks as they prove.
Cover, rise 30–60 min until puffy. Oven to 220 °C, bring the boiling water up.
Boil each bagel 1 min per side, lift out, top with seeds while wet.
Bake 20–25 min to deep gold. Cool on a rack.

title: Discard sandwich loaf
steps: Whisk water, honey and yeast; stand 5 min until bubbly.
Everything into the mixer, knead ~10 min until it passes the windowpane test.
Greased bowl, 1–2 h until doubled.
Press into a rectangle, roll up tightly, pinch the ends, seam-down in a greased loaf tin.
Second rise 30–60 min. Bake at 190 °C for 45 min — core temperature 93–99 °C.
Cool completely before slicing, or it gums up.

title: Sourdough pasta
steps: Three ingredients into the mixer with a dough hook, 10 min on low–medium until smooth and stretchy.
Rest 30 min — non-negotiable, or it fights the rolling pin.
Divide into 8, roll each as thin as you dare on a floured surface.
Roll the sheet up loosely and cut across with a sharp knife into ribbons.
Hang or lay out to dry 30 min to 2 h, then boil 4–5 min, stirring to separate.
asides: For a real ferment: leave the dough covered 2–6 h, then chill up to 24 h before rolling.

title: Skillet flatbread
steps: Mix discard, flour, milk and salt; knead briefly to bring it together.
Cover and leave 2–4 h, or overnight for more sourness.
Divide into 8, roll each to about 6 mm.
Olive oil in a medium-hot cast-iron pan, 1–2 min a side until lightly spotted.
asides: Water or oat milk instead of dairy works fine. Doubles as a pizza base or a wrap.

title: Naan
steps: Mix flour, baking powder and salt in one bowl.
Whisk milk, yoghurt, sugar and discard in another.
Bring together into a shaggy dough, then knead briefly on the counter until mostly smooth.
Oiled bowl, covered, somewhere warm for 5–6 h until doubled.
Divide into 8, roll into 15 cm ovals.
Medium-hot pan, 60–90 seconds a side. Brush with melted butter off the heat.

title: Soft discard rolls
ingredients: 56 g butter, melted and cooled (¼ cup)
steps: Whisk yeast and warm water in the mixer bowl, cover 5 min until foamy.
Add discard, sugar, butter, salt and flour; mix low 2 min.
Step up a gear and knead 5–10 min until smooth, glossy and windowpaning.
Greased bowl, covered, 60–90 min until doubled.
Divide into 8, shape tight balls, sit them in a greased 20 × 20 cm dish, rise 30–60 min.
Oven to 190 °C, egg wash, bake 25–30 min. Butter the tops straight out of the oven.

title: Tortillas
steps: Knead everything 2–3 min in a mixer, or 5 min by hand, until slightly elastic.
Greased bowl, tea towel over the top, 12–24 h at room temperature. Go the full 24 h if you want the gentlest version.
Divide into 12 and roll each one as thin as it will go without tearing.
Hot cast iron with a smear of oil, 1 min a side. Stack them under a towel to stay soft.

title: Crumpets
steps: Beat discard, flour, salt, water and sugar 2–3 min to a smooth batter. Cover, leave at room temperature 12 h.
Medium heat, half the butter in the pan; butter the inside of the rings and set them in.
Sprinkle the Natron over the batter and stir it smooth — this is what opens the holes.
Fill each ring, cook 8–10 min until the tops set with visible holes and the base is golden.
Lift the rings off, serve warm. Repeat with the rest of the butter and batter.

title: Rosemary focaccia
steps: In the mixer, combine starter, water, half the oil, honey and salt.
Add the flour gradually until the dough pulls away from the bowl, then knead 10 min or more until it windowpanes.
Greased bowl, covered, room temperature until puffy and up by about half — 4–12 h.
Pour the other half of the oil into a parchment-lined tray. Press the dough right out to the edges.
Cover, rise 1–2 h until puffy. Dimple it with your fingertips, drizzle more oil, scatter garlic powder and rosemary.
Bake 20–25 min at 220 °C until golden.

title: Soft sourdough buns
ingredients: 56 g melted butter or coconut oil (¼ cup)
steps: Everything except the glaze into the mixer with a dough hook; knead 5–10 min until smooth and elastic.
Greased bowl, covered, 8 h at room temperature.
Into the fridge overnight, still covered.
Divide into 8. Shape each with a flat top, edges tucked under, spinning it on the counter to build tension.
Cover, rise 1–2 h until doubled.
Egg wash, sesame if you want them, bake 25–30 min at 175 °C to deep gold.
asides: A low, gentle oven — these are meant to stay soft, not crust.

title: Artisan boule
steps: Feed the starter 4–12 h ahead — it should double or triple and float.
Mix flour, salt, starter and water. Knead to a windowpane, or leave it in the bowl and do stretch-and-folds instead.
Oiled bowl, tightly covered, bulk ferment 8–24 h until doubled. A warm kitchen puts you at the fast end of that.
Shape into a round, seam-side up in a floured banneton.
Second rise 2–4 h at room temperature — or 12–15 h in the fridge, which gives a better crumb and much easier scoring.
Preheat the Dutch oven at 260 °C for a full hour. This is the step people skip and then wonder why the loaf is flat.
Tip onto parchment, score, lower it in. 20 min covered ; uncover, drop to 230 °C, 20 min more.
asides: The one to learn first. Four ingredients, a wide fermentation window, and it tolerates being mistimed.

title: Ciabatta rolls
steps: Combine starter, water, salt and flour; rest 30 min. It will feel far too wet — at 79 % that's correct.
Three sets of stretch-and-folds, 30 min apart.
Leave until doubled, about 4 h.
Cover and refrigerate 12–24 h.
Tip onto a well-floured surface and coax into a rectangle. Cut lengthways, then each half into four. Handle it as little as you can — the big irregular holes are the whole point.
Lift onto parchment, cover, rise 1–2 h.
Preheat with a cast-iron pan on the bottom shelf. Load the rolls, pour water into the hot pan for steam, bake 25 min.

title: Caraway rye
steps: Mix everything, cover, rest 30 min.
Six sets of stretch-and-folds: the first three 15 min apart, the last three 30 min apart.
Bulk ferment covered until doubled — up to 12 h. Rye ferments faster than wheat, so start checking early.
Shape into a ball and leave it uncovered 15–20 min to form a skin.
Reshape, seam-side up in a floured banneton, cover, fridge 12–15 h.
Dutch oven preheated at 245 °C for an hour. Score, bake 20 min covered, 20 min uncovered.
asides: Molasses and caraway do the heavy lifting here — with Roggenmehl Type 1150 you're close to a German Mischbrot.

title: 100 % whole wheat
ingredients: 475 g whole wheat flour, freshly milled if you have it
steps: Mix water, starter, salt and flour by hand for 5 min in a big bowl.
Damp towel over the top, rest 1 h. Wholemeal drinks slowly — this hour is what stops the dough feeling dry and tearing.
Six rounds of stretch-and-fold: lift one side up about 15 cm and fold it over, quarter-turn, four times a round. First three rounds 15 min apart, last three 30 min apart.
Bulk ferment somewhere warm until doubled — roughly 8 h.
Shape into a ball, dragging it against the counter for tension. Rest uncovered 15–20 min.
Reshape into a floured banneton, cover, fridge 12–14 h.
Dutch oven at 260 °C for a full hour. Score it cold, bake 20 min covered, 20 min uncovered. Cool completely before cutting.
asides: No white flour to fall back on, so the bran cuts the gluten and the loaf is denser by nature. Judge it by feel, not by clock.
